latest_release.name: RuView toolkit 0.9.2
latest_release.body:
@ruvnet/ruview 0.9.2

Maintenance fixes from [PR #2248](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/pull/2248), which records the exact source heads for 38 integrated contributor PRs.

- Accept official C6 firmware bundle filenames while preserving checksum and board-variant validation.
- Correct CSI loss accounting, observed capture duration, dominant stream selection, and synthetic-data provenance; reject malformed auxiliary packets.
- Correct ESPHome units and entity roles, report incomplete serial captures, and fix LiDAR/mmWave summaries and stream completion.
- Validate CLI numeric arguments, preserve gaps in watch history, report corrupt manifests through doctor, and honor SDK strict errors.
- Replace inherited and explicit Windows hosts-file ACL grants with verified current-user-only access. Paths are passed as data to the bounded helper, including Unicode and shell-special characters.
- Preserve source recordings during transcoding, avoid capture-session filename collisions, and retain complete relayed UDP datagrams.
- Exercise the contributor harness on Linux and Windows and correct CI snapshot release metadata.

Install the exact package with `npm install @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.2`, or run its CLI using `npx @ruvnet/ruview@0.9.2 --help`.

Repository-only changes also improve Home Assistant client topic compatibility and the MTK bridge test lifecycle. These changes do not imply that a new Python wheel or hardware-qualified firmware was published with this npm package.

The release commit also contains the separately reviewed [calibration and sensing fixes](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/pull/2246): failed recording or baseline-save sessions finish as aborted, and diagnostic fields follow the actual occupancy decision without changing the accepted decision rules.

Compatible board images are available separately in the [ESP32 firmware 0.8.14 prerelease](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/releases/tag/v0.8.14-esp32). Its S3 8 MB, S3 4 MB, and C6 4 MB bundles have verified archive and image checksums. They have CI build and host-test coverage, with no new physical-board qualification.

Published by the [npm release workflow](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/actions/runs/38280634481) from commit [`0f95193190261a8966ad5f52e188aa6a480c2968`](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuView/commit/0f95193190261a8966ad5f52e188aa6a480c2968). Registry signatures and the provenance attestation verified successfully and bind the downloaded tarball to this exact commit and workflow. The attached tarball is identical to the tested, published npm package; verify it with the attached `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

A fresh installation passed package-manifest, CLI, SDK, and read-only firmware-bundle checks for all three published board variants. No hardware operations were performed. No learning proposal or experimental Dream Machine candidate is promoted by this release.

## **See through walls with WiFi** ## **Turn ordinary WiFi into a spatial intelligence / sensing system.** Detect people, measure breathing and heart rate, track movement, and monitor rooms — through walls, in the dark, with no cameras or wearables. Just physics. Works natively with the four major smart-home ecosystems: **[Home Assistant](docs/integrations/home-assistant.md)** via the HA-DISCO MQTT publisher, **[Apple Home & HomePod](docs/user-guide-apple-homepod.md)** as a discoverable HAP-1.1 bridge, **[Google Home](docs/integrations/home-assistant.md)** + **[Amazon Alexa](docs/integrations/home-assistant.md)** via the same HA bridge or a [Matter](docs/adr/ADR-122-bfld-ruview-ha-matter-exposure.md) endpoint. Siri, Google Assistant, and Alexa can voice presence and vitals by room with zero custom skills.
